rows.blocker_closure_criterion: Both: (1) the real wire width (1 vs 2 sixteen-bit registers) is confirmed by an official errata/clarification or a controlled protocol-capture experiment on a lab-safe device, per protocol/evidence/protocol_blockers.json's own VoltageCalibration (0x1600) entry; AND (2) the exact payload encoding (does the command take the calibration reference voltage in mV as its raw integer value, some other scale, or a fixed trigger constant?) is established by the same means -- the official PDF and V2 workbook state only the register's existence, access=W, wire type, and unit (mV); neither gives a worked example or a prose description of what value to write. Until both hold, this command is never implemented, never has a production endpoint, and this project never fabricates either the width or the payload value.

The exact trigger payload (e.g. a specific magic value such as 0x0001, vs. 'any non-zero write triggers shutdown', vs. some other fixed code) is established by an official errata/clarification or a controlled protocol-capture experiment on a lab-safe device. The official PDF and V2 workbook confirm only the register's address/access=W/wire type/length (UINT16, 2 bytes, internally consistent -- no width ambiguity here) and the command's PURPOSE ('forced BMS board shutdown'); neither states what value the command register actually expects. Guessing a trigger value for a command that cuts board power is exactly the fabrication this Stage explicitly forbids.

Same two-part criterion as voltage_calibration (0x1600), resolved independently for this address: (1) real wire width (1 vs 2 registers) and (2) exact payload encoding (calibration reference current in mA as raw integer, another scale, or a fixed trigger constant) both confirmed by official clarification or a controlled protocol-capture experiment. See protocol/evidence/protocol_blockers.json's CurrentCalibration (0x1606) entry.

The exact trigger payload for applying the Li-ion (NMC/NCA) chemistry preset is established by official clarification or a controlled protocol-capture experiment. Width (UINT16, 2 bytes) is internally consistent and not in question; the VALUE that actually triggers the preset (vs. leaves the register merely 'writable but inert') is not stated anywhere in the local sources. This command silently rewrites safety-critical protection thresholds for the wrong chemistry if triggered incorrectly -- never guessed.
Same criterion as li_ion (0x160A), resolved independently for this address's LiFePO4 chemistry preset trigger value.
Same criterion as li_ion (0x160A), resolved independently for this address's LTO (lithium titanate) chemistry preset trigger value.

The exact trigger payload for the emergency forced-discharge-MOS-open override is established by official clarification or a controlled protocol-capture experiment. Width (UINT16, 2 bytes) is internally consistent; the register also has an associated READ-side status/timer field (0x12A0's own 应急开关时间/TimeEmergency at a different address) that this canonical entry deliberately does not conflate with -- that is a separate, already-canonical read field, not evidence of this write command's own trigger value.

A unit of seconds is stated only by the V2 workbook (row 254, column E 'секунди (S)'), not by the official PDF, whose unit cell for this row is empty; a unit is in any case not an encoding, and the exact reference/encoding is not established: is the written UINT32 a Unix epoch timestamp, seconds since an unstated device-specific epoch, or a relative/delta value? The official PDF states only 'UINT32, 4 bytes, W, 对时/Timecalibration' with no unit, no worked example and no epoch definition. Writing an assumed epoch (e.g. guessing Unix time) to a real BMS RTC without source confirmation is exactly the fabricated-payload-value case this Stage forbids, even though a unit is stated here (by the V2 workbook only) unlike for the other 7 commands. The register WORD ORDER of this 2-register UINT32 is equally unestablished (word_order=null): no source states it for 0x1612, and the high-word-first order shown by the PDF's worked FC16 frames for other UINT32 registers (base 0x1000) is not transferred to this address by inference. Resolved by an official clarification of the epoch/reference point AND the word order, or a controlled protocol-capture experiment comparing a written value against the BMS's own subsequently-read wall-clock behavior.
